Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

trend noun

the way things are going

also tendency, the trend is towards, tend towards, be heading for, trends

classical

Liv. 1.9.6: ad vim spectāre rēs coepit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 14.5.1: ad arma rem spectāre (Lewis & Short)

spectāre ad

phrase: rēs as the subject, ad with the accusative

tend towards, be heading for (of how things are going)

Latin says where things are heading rather than naming a trend. The verb’s first sense is “look at, watch”; Lewis & Short gives this sense as “to tend, incline, refer”.

Other words

  • inclīnātiō, inclīnātiōnis f. — a turn, a shift (of the times); a tendency

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 6.10.5: inclīnātiōnēs temporum atque momenta (Lewis & Short); Traupman 397

    Literally a leaning, a bending. Lewis & Short: figuratively an inclination or tendency (ad meliōrem spem, Cic. Sest. 67), a bias or favour, and a change in the times. Traupman’s word for “trend”. For a trend in fashion, see style.

Examples

  • ad vim spectāre rēs coepit

    things began to head towards violenceLiv. 1.9.6 (Lewis & Short)

  • nisi forte rēbus cūnctīs inest quīdam velut orbis, ut quem ad modum temporum vicēs ita mōrum vertantur

    unless perhaps there is a kind of cycle in all things, so that ways of life change as the seasons doTac. Ann. 3.55

See also style, change, pattern, situation.

SourcesLewis & Short: specto · Lewis & Short: inclinatio
